paper_design_summary: The paper evaluates the Semantic Repulsion Technique (SRT) in three model-only experiments: a five-system comparison, a mechanism ablation, and a lambda sweep (pp. 5–7, Sections 4.1–4.3). A within-subjects user study has 16 participants who regularly use AI for creative tasks review one response from each of four systems across three tasks and rate originality, coherence, creativity, and usefulness on 5-point Likert scales (pp. 7–9, Section 4.4). The procedure does not state who supplied prompts or when outputs were generated, and no participant-produced creative output is reported as scored (p. 8, Section 4.4, Procedure).

Participants rated each output on 5-point Likert scales for originality, coherence, creativity, and usefulness.

Section 4.2 reports Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons of C7 versus C0 as p < 0.001 across all metrics and modes; no individual originality test statistics are printed.

eligibility.reason: The user study analyzes 16 people (p. 7, Section 4.4; p. 9, Table 4), below the 50-person eligibility threshold; the same people rate all four systems (p. 8, Procedure). The procedure reports a within-subjects evaluation of AI-generated responses, with no stated random assignment of AI assistance or system order. It does not state who supplied the prompts or when responses were generated, and no participant-produced creative output is reported as scored (p. 8, Section 4.4). The three computational experiments (S2–S4) are model-only (pp. 5–7, Sections 4.1–4.3; pp. 11–14, Appendices A–D). These model-only experiments and the human evaluation of AI-made work do not qualify for the core dataset or any context class. Retain them in the screening report and omit them from the dataset.

one_line_finding: In a 16-person within-subjects rating study, SRT-Strong outputs were rated more useful (M = 3.60 vs 3.10 for Baseline-Pure; Friedman p = .019) and more coherent (3.92 vs 3.48; p = .006) than baseline outputs, with a non-significant originality difference (3.40 vs 2.85; p = .062) (pp. 8-9, Section 4.4).
notes: The three model-only experiments are recorded separately. Their outcomes answer none of the three human-assistance questions; the computational entries retain compact descriptive summaries of originality/diversity. Other reported computational diagnostics include consensus phrase frequency, relevance, and coherence/perplexity (Sections 4.1–4.3; Appendix C). Generated-output totals and per-cell counts are not participant counts. In S3 and S4, n_units records the full experiment corpus, while reported contrast cell sizes are stated separately. The "nine values" wording in Section 4.3, p. 6 conflicts with its five-value list, the continuation on p. 7, and Tables 3 and 9; S4 records the five enumerated and tabulated values.
